claim_details.claim: Current scientific research is divided on whether fish can feel pain like humans. Some studies, including work by Dr. Lynne Sneddon, argue that fish do feel pain based on the presence of pain receptors in the brain and the fact that fish modify their behavior in response to noxious stimuli

However, other researchers, including Dr. Rose of the University of Wyoming, contend that the experience of pain in fish is very different from that of humans — that fish lack the neocortex (the brain region associated with conscious experience in mammals) and that their response to noxious stimuli is best described as nociception rather than pain

A prominent peer-reviewed review published in Frontiers in Zoology further complicates the picture, noting that while fish do respond to noxious stimuli, this does not necessarily entail that they experience the stimuli subjectively as humans do
